title: Collaboration: Keep Read Receipts Monotonic Across Devices
businessContext: An old mobile receipt arrives after a desktop receipt and increases the unread badge. Another user’s receipt is mistakenly applied locally.
problemStatement: Implement solution({ userId, lastRead, highWater, updates }). lastRead/highWater are safe integers with 0 <= lastRead <= highWater. Each update is an object. A nonmatching userId => forbidden before validation. For this user, sequence must be a safe integer in [0,highWater], otherwise invalid. sequence <= current lastRead => stale; otherwise advance and return advanced. Return { lastRead, unread:highWater-lastRead, outcomes }. Empty updates leave the receipt unchanged.
constraints: Implement the synchronous solution(input) contract exactly. Do not mutate input; all inputs are JSON data.
This is a deterministic state model. It does not open sockets, send notifications, authorize real users, or establish media connections.
candidateTasks: Reproduce the starter failure, implement the invariant, and pass every authored case.
How would you atomically merge read positions across devices while excluding messages the recipient cannot see?
starterCode: function solution({lastRead,highWater,updates}) { for(const u of updates) lastRead=u.sequence; return {lastRead,unread:highWater-lastRead,outcomes:updates.map(()=>'advanced')}; }

testCases.name: Reject other user before sequence validation
Reject future negative fractional and string sequences
Out of order updates never regress

hints: Write down validation and replay precedence before changing state.
Use stable IDs and monotonic sequence/version values; preserve input ownership.
alternativeApproaches: Use an append-only event log with transactional projections.
Use a database snapshot plus a versioned resume cursor.
commonMistakes: Trusting delivery order or treating retries as new operations.
Mutating caller-owned arrays or accepting cross-channel data.
Presenting a fixture result as a guarantee of real-time delivery or media connectivity.
